post.caption: Rolex's Daytona engine hid in an attic. Zenith launched its El Primero chronograph movement in 1969,. An American radio company bought Zenith in 1971, and in 1975 the owners decided to stop making it. A watchmaker named Charles Vermot hid the plans and tools in a walled off part of the factory attic, including 150 presses. Years later, Rolex wanted a self winding chronograph for its Daytona. The first Zenith powered Daytonas appeared in 1988, and the El Primero ran in the Daytona until 2000.
